interface.name: list_orders
interface.title: List Store Orders
interface.description: Returns a paginated list of the store's orders with each order's reference number, date, status, total and customer, optionally narrowed by status, by a date range, or by a keyword.
whenToUse: The merchant wants to see recent orders, e.g. 'show me my latest orders' or 'what came in today?'.

The merchant asks about orders in a particular state, e.g. 'what's still awaiting review?' or 'list recent shipped orders' -- call list_order_statuses first to turn the merchant's wording into this store's status id, then filter with the status argument.
The merchant asks about a period, e.g. 'orders from last week' or 'what did I get in March?' -- filter with fromDate and toDate.
The merchant is looking for one customer's orders by name or mobile number, or for an order by its shipping number or reference id -- filter with the keyword argument.
An agent needs order ids or reference numbers before reporting on or acting on specific orders.
whenNotToUse: The merchant named ONE specific order and wants its full details, line items or shipping -- use get_order with the order id instead.
The merchant wants to know which order states the store has, rather than the orders themselves -- use list_order_statuses instead.
The merchant wants to move an order to a different state -- this tool only reads; use update_order_status instead.
The merchant is asking about the catalogue rather than what has been bought -- use list_products instead.

page.description: Pagination page number. The response returns one page of orders; increment to fetch the rest.

status.description: Return only orders in these states, given as this store's own status ids -- the `id` field of a row from list_order_statuses. NOT slugs, NOT status names, and NOT the canonical id under `original`: the upstream silently returns zero orders for the wrong kind of id, which reads as an empty store rather than as an error. The ids are per-store, so they must be looked up and cannot be recalled or guessed.

fromDate.description: Earliest order date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD.

toDate.description: Latest order date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD.

keyword.description: Find orders by customer name or mobile number, shipping number, reference id, or tag name.

id.description: The order id, used by sibling order tools.

reference_id.description: The order number the merchant and the customer see; quote this one back to a merchant, not the id.

timezone.description: The store's timezone the timestamp is expressed in, e.g. 'Asia/Riyadh'.

status.description: The state the order is currently in.

id.description: The CANONICAL Salla status id, the same across every store. Note this is not the id the status filter above takes -- that one is under `customized`.

name.description: The status as the merchant sees it, in the store's own language -- often Arabic.

slug.description: The canonical state family, e.g. 'under_review'. Readable, and safe to report to a merchant, but not unique across a store's custom states and not accepted by the status filter.

customized.description: This store's own version of the state -- {id, name}. Its id is the one the status argument takes and the one list_order_statuses returns as `id`.

name.description: The store's own name for the state.

payment_method.description: How the order was paid, e.g. 'bank' or 'credit_card'.

mobile.description: The customer's mobile number, without the country code held in mobile_code.

city.description: The customer's city, in the store's own language.

http.summary: List Orders -- list all orders related to your store, filterable by status, date range, and a keyword matching customer name or mobile, shipping number, reference id or tag.

query.name: status
query.description: The store's own order status ids to filter by. Salla takes this as an array, serialized Laravel-style as status[]=1&status[]=2.

query.name: keyword
query.description: A keyword matched against customer name and mobile, shipping number, reference id and tag name.

statuses.meaning: The store's access token is missing, expired, or does not carry the orders.read scope, so the store's orders cannot be read until the app's authorization is fixed.

rules.message: fromDate must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD form
toDate must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD form

dependencies.reason: the status filter takes this store's own status ids, which are per-store and cannot be guessed -- list_order_statuses is the only place they come from
